_note: Regime anchors for the record-to-parcel cardinality guard (scripts/check_value_anchors.py). Bands, not equalities: assessed values move every reassessment. See docs/FINDINGS_lot_dedupe.md and docs/FINDINGS_denominator_cardinality.md.
_bands_are_per_anchor: ⚠️ THESE BANDS ARE NO LONGER UNIFORM AND `--write-baseline` WOULD FLATTEN THEM. That flag applies ONE global --tolerance (default 0.5) to every anchor, which is exactly what this file stopped doing on 2026-08-05. If you re-pin with it, re-apply the split below by hand or the drift guard silently loosens back to ±50%.
_why_two_widths: Set 2026-08-05 from the first real variance data: every anchor value the guard has logged in CI since it shipped (5 runs, but only 3 INDEPENDENT data changes — 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-05 committed status.json only, so their readings re-measure unchanged input). FOUR anchors were effectively frozen across that window (dup_parcel_points constant at 33; dedupe_effect_pct 0.01% spread; dup_parcel_value_frac 0.11%; lot_needle_ratio 0.00%) and were tightened 2x, to ±25% of the latest reading. TWO were NOT tightened because they are not noisy, they are TRENDING — see _ineligible_pair_is_drifting.
_why_only_25_percent: ⚠️ NOT tightened to the observed spread (~0.1%), deliberately. The guard exists mainly for the January year-roll (docs/RUNBOOK.md), and NO OBSERVATION ACROSS A YEAR-ROLL EXISTS YET — the guard shipped 2026-07-28. Three weekly observations say nothing about how these move on reassessment, so ±25% buys a real 2x tightening while leaving room for the event the guard was built for. Revisit after the first January roll, which is the observation that would justify going tighter.
_ineligible_pair_is_drifting: ⚠️ ineligible_points AND ineligible_value_frac WERE LEFT AT ±50% ON PURPOSE — DO NOT 'FINISH THE JOB' BY TIGHTENING THEM. They moved on EVERY independent data change, monotonically upward, with no reversal: ineligible_points 56 -> 58 -> 60 and ineligible_value_frac 0.00517 -> 0.00575 -> 0.00633 across 2026-08-01 / 08-03 / 08-04. That is the DANGEROUS direction by this guard's own definition (DANGER['ineligible_*'] == 'high': growth means more value silently leaving the lot-acre denominator). ineligible_value_frac has already consumed ~72% of its band and would breach in roughly 2-3 more moves of the observed size. Tightening it would red the weekly publish on the next real data change and read as a false alarm; the band is left wide so that when it does fire, it fires on a genuine regime shift. The cause is an OPEN TODO item.
_lot_needle_is_now_one_cell: ⚠️ RE-PINNED 2026-09-01 for the 50 m Glass grid (was 9.616-16.027 at 100 m; live reading moved 12 -> 79.01). THE MOVE IS RESOLUTION, NOT DATA — halving the cell stopped diluting a defect that was always there. The top cell is 3 WESTMOUNT condo records (accounts 4259396/4259412/4259420, $859,500 assessed) whose lot_size reads 0.505/0.218/0.277 — ownership SHARES summing to 1.000, not m². At 100 m that cell merged with neighbours holding real lots and the needle vanished entirely; at 50 m it is the top cell in the city. ⚠️ BAND IS +/-50%, NOT the +/-25% the four 'frozen' anchors use — DO NOT TIGHTEN IT TO MATCH THEM. That 25% was earned by anchors observed flat across independent data changes; this anchor's value is now set by ONE degenerate record, so its stability across a reassessment is unobserved and probably poor. Tightening would red the weekly publish on a single upstream edit. Revisit only after the sub-1 m2 lot_size defect is fixed (docs/DATA_ISSUES.md) or the first January roll, whichever lands first.
